steps.content:
All eyes in the room are pulled, as if by a grim gravity, to the object at its center.
It is a thing of crude, cast-iron utility—unadorned, cold, and heavy. A palpable aura of doom seeps from its rough surface.

The silence is not silent at all. It is filled with the low, wasp-like buzz of electricity and the tight, strained breathing of the crowd. Against the backdrop of the rain, these sounds become a symphony of anxiety.
<color=#dg1f1f>1:57:03</color>
With every tiny decrement of the numbers, a minute click echoes from within, a sound so small it seems to be heard by the bones more than the ears, and it sends a visceral shiver through you.
Hilda's eyes trace the lines of the iron coffin, now monstrously changed, her demeanor unnervingly placid.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I'm staying to disarm it.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: What?!

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Have you lost your mind, Hilda! That's not the Monolith anymore, it's a bomb! You have barely two hours!

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: The plan has failed! Our only objective now is to evacuate immediately and inform the superiors!

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: We haven't failed yet.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: It's just a temporary "bomb." Once disarmed, its core functionality will remain intact.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: The city-state is waiting for the intelligence Monolith is meant to carry. We cannot abandon our mission at the final moment.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: If it explodes, we lose everything.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: ...Insane. You're insane.
Helene stumbles backward, bumping into you.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: You're all insane, but I'm not! I'm done with this! I'm getting out of here! I refuse to die in this damned place!
She shoves you aside and rushes upstairs.
[Room]

Helene stumbles to her desk, yanking the drawer open with a violent screech. She claws through its contents—a jumble of undergarments, dog-eared foreign magazines, and cosmetics—sending it all flying across the floor.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: This is crazy! I only came here for a damn seminar. I am NOT going to die in this place.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: I have to survive... I am going to make it back alive...
Soon, her frantic fingers hit the back of the drawer, finding two cold, hard objects.
She pulls them out with trembling hands: an antique brass bird whistle and an unsealed kraft paper envelope.
[Main Hall]

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Helene, calm down!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The mole just made their move, and now you're demanding to leave? You'll make yourself the prime suspect!
In a burst of anger, Helene heaves her travel bag down.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: I don't have time for your witch hunt anymore!

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: I still don't know what I did to deserve being dragged into this hellhole. Unless I've somehow slept with the mole, I am the most innocent person here!

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: You know me, Officer! You know I'm not clever enough for these kinds of games!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You need to face reality. I'm trying to help you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I know you're terrified. I know you want to run. But you've worked with Hilda longer than I have. You, more than me, should trust her capabilities.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When has she ever failed to solve a puzzle?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Even in the worst-case scenario, I will get you out myself. But right now, you need to stay.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: ...Ha... Pretty words.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: In my line of work, you hear all kinds of sweet talk. "Stay with me tonight." "Marry me, you'll be the happiest woman alive." Some promises are sincere, others are lies, and I have a talent for believing the lies.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: I'll be frank with you, Officer... Someone proposed to me. He found out my identity. He knows I'm a spy for the metropoles! And he said he didn't care. He still wanted to love me, to wait for me, to run away with me.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: I was paralyzed. I couldn't bring myself to silence him, but I couldn't bring myself to defect, either. And that's when the orders came down for this seminar.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: I just want... a chance to choose again...

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Don't stand in my way. Once I'm safe, I'll burn that letter myself.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: But if you try to stop me, I'll expose your secret right away. I mean it.
She wipes away her tears and rudely pushes past you, her high heels striking the marble floor with rapid, frantic clicks. She rushes toward the iron door, toward her gateway to freedom.
[Exterior/The Garden]
Rain pours down in sheets, but Helene doesn't wonder if any birds will respond. Her hands tremble as she raises the cold brass bird whistle to her pale lips.
Whoooo—chirrup-chirrup—chirrurup-chirrurup—
The crisp, resonant call slices through the deathly silence of the rain. It sounds like a desperate cry for help, a stark contrast to the grim surroundings.

Miraculously, moments later, wings flutter from the bare crowns of the plane trees. A few startled sparrows flee. Then, a more agile, familiar white shape dives gracefully down and lands precisely on Helene's trembling fingertips.
It is a snow-white messenger pigeon. In the dim light, its eyes gleam like two smooth black obsidian stones.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Good... good little bird...

Her voice breaks as she fumbles with the small brass ring on the pigeon's leg. She opens the miniature bamboo tube and, with trembling fingers, carefully rolls her note and inserts it into the tiny container, sealing it tightly.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Good little bird... take this to him for me. He promised to love me forever, didn't he? He said he would pluck the stars and moon from the sky for me... so let him come save me now.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Go, little bird, fly! Hurry, fly away—

She thrusts the pigeon upward with all her might. Its pure white wings spread against the gloomy sky like hope breaking free from despair. The bird circles once, seems to find its bearings, and flies away.
Yet in that very moment, as hope takes flight—
A dark figure stands in the doorway shadows, having been silently watching for who knows how long.
Hilda's right hand rises with absolute steadiness.
The cold wind sweeps at the hem of her dark wool coat. She stands expressionless, her face like the surface of a frozen lake. Only her eyes are alive, blood-red and predatory.
The gun barrel in her hand catches the dim light, gleaming with a cold, lethal shine.
You decide to...

options: You don't need to kill her.
